question: If they work properly, they will not be punished. (Rewrite using 'unless')
answers: Unless they work properly, they will be punished.
Unless they work properly they will be punished.
hint: 'If' ki jagah 'Unless' lagayein aur doosre clause se 'not' hata dein kyunki 'unless' khud negative hota hai.
explanation: 'Unless' ka matlab 'If...not' hota hai. Isliye 'If' ko 'Unless' se badalne par doosre clause ka 'not' hatakar 'they will be punished' likha jayega.

question: Unless they work properly they will be punished. (Rewrite using 'if')
answers: If they do not work properly, they will be punished.
If they do not work properly they will be punished.
If they don't work properly, they will be punished.
If they don't work properly they will be punished.
hint: 'Unless' hatakar 'If' lagayein aur Present Indefinite tense ke anusaar 'do not' jodein.
explanation: Sentence Present Indefinite me hai aur subject 'they' plural hai, isliye 'Unless' ki jagah 'If they do not work properly' ka use hoga.

question: If you do not work hard, you cannot pass. (Rewrite using 'unless')
answers: Unless you work hard, you cannot pass.
Unless you work hard you cannot pass.
Unless you work hard, you can't pass.
Unless you work hard you can't pass.
hint: 'If...do not' ko hatakar uski jagah sirf 'Unless' lagayein; doosre clause me koi badlav nahi hoga.
explanation: 'If you do not' ko 'Unless you' me badal diya jata hai aur doosra clause 'you cannot pass' waisa hi rehta hai.

question: You will miss the train if you don't hurry. (Rewrite using 'unless')
answers: You will miss the train unless you hurry.
hint: 'if you don't' ki jagah 'unless you' ka use karein.
explanation: 'if you don't hurry' me se 'if' aur 'don't' hatakar 'unless you hurry' likhne se sentence ka arth wahi rehta hai.

question: Unless you invite me, I will not come. (Rewrite using 'if')
answers: If you do not invite me, I will not come.
If you do not invite me I will not come.
If you don't invite me, I will not come.
If you don't invite me, I won't come.
If you do not invite me, I won't come.
hint: 'Unless you' ko hatakar Present Indefinite me 'If you do not' lagayein.
explanation: 'Unless' hatane par negative arth banaye rakhne ke liye 'If you do not invite me' ka use kiya jata hai.

question: He is too poor to pay his fees. (Rewrite using 'so...that')
answers: He is so poor that he cannot pay his fees.
He is so poor that he can't pay his fees.
hint: 'too' ki jagah 'so' lagayein aur 'to' ki jagah 'that + Subject + cannot' (Present tense hone ke karan) likhein.
explanation: Sentence 'is' (Present tense) me hai, isliye 'too...to' ko hatakar 'so poor that he cannot pay his fees' banega.

question: This box is too heavy to be lifted. (Rewrite using 'so...that')
answers: This box is so heavy that it cannot be lifted.
This box is so heavy that it can't be lifted.
hint: 'This box' ke liye pronoun 'it' ka use karein aur Present tense me 'cannot' lagayein.
explanation: 'too' ko 'so' me badlein aur 'to be lifted' ko 'that it cannot be lifted' me change karein.

question: This question is so difficult that we cannot learn it. (Replace 'so...that' with 'too...to')
answers: This question is too difficult for us to learn.
hint: 'so' ki jagah 'too' lagayein aur 'that we cannot' ko 'for us to' me badlein (aakhir se 'it' hata dein).
explanation: 'so difficult that we cannot learn it' ko 'too...to' me badalne par 'too difficult for us to learn' sahi structure banta hai.

question: As soon as the teacher left the class, the students started shouting. (Use 'no sooner...than')
answers: No sooner did the teacher leave the class than the students started shouting.
hint: Past Indefinite ('left') hone par 'No sooner did + Subject + V1' aur comma ki jagah 'than' lagta hai.
explanation: 'left' V2 hai, isliye 'No sooner did the teacher leave' (V1) aayega aur dono clauses ko jodne ke liye 'than' lagega.

question: As soon as he saw the police, he ran away. (Use 'no sooner...than')
answers: No sooner did he see the police than he ran away.
hint: 'did' ke saath verb ki first form ('see') aati hai aur 'No sooner' ke saath 'than' lagta hai.
explanation: 'saw' Past Indefinite hai, isliye 'No sooner did he see the police' banega aur comma hatakar 'than' lagega.

question: As soon as Sunit gets salary he starts spending it. (Use 'No sooner...than')
answers: No sooner does Sunit get salary than he starts spending it.
No sooner does Sunit get his salary than he starts spending it.
hint: 'gets' Present Indefinite hai, isliye 'No sooner does + Subject + V1' ka use hoga.
explanation: Present Indefinite aur singular subject 'Sunit' ke karan 'No sooner does Sunit get salary' aayega aur 'than' se doosra clause judega.

question: As soon as he closed his eyes, the telephone rang. (Use 'no sooner...than')
answers: No sooner did he close his eyes than the telephone rang.
hint: 'closed' Past Indefinite hai, isliye 'did' ke saath V1 ('close') aur 'than' ka use karein.
explanation: 'As soon as he closed' ko 'No sooner did he close' me badlein aur comma ki jagah 'than' lagayein.

question: We will leave. We finish our work. (Combine using 'as soon as')
answers: We will leave as soon as we finish our work.
As soon as we finish our work, we will leave.
hint: 'as soon as' wale clause me Future tense ('will') ka use nahi hota, wahan Simple Present hi rehta hai.
explanation: Dono sentences ko jodne par 'We will leave as soon as we finish our work' sahi banega ('as soon as' ke baad Simple Present use hota hai).

question: He makes nice tea. (Change the Voice)
answers: Nice tea is made by him.
hint: Simple Present Passive structure: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject.
explanation: 'makes' Simple Present tense hai, isliye Passive me 'is made' aur 'He' ka 'by him' hoga.

question: Ravi knows him. (Change the Voice)
answers: He is known to Ravi.
hint: Passive voice me 'known' ke baad 'by' ki jagah hamesha preposition 'to' lagta hai.
explanation: 'knows' Simple Present hai aur 'know' verb ke saath passive me 'by' nahi balki 'to' ('known to') ka use hota hai.

question: What are you reading? (Change the Voice)
answers: What is being read by you?
hint: Present Continuous Interrogative Passive: What + is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject?
explanation: Present Continuous ('are reading') ka passive banate waqt 'is being read' (V3) ka use kiya jata hai.

question: They are not playing football. (Make passive)
answers: Football is not being played by them.
Football isn't being played by them.
hint: Present Continuous Negative Passive: Object + is/am/are + not + being + V3 + by + Subject.
explanation: 'Football' singular object hai aur sentence Present Continuous me hai, isliye 'is not being played by them' sahi hoga.

question: Mona writes a letter. (Change the Voice)
answers: A letter is written by Mona.
hint: 'writes' Simple Present tense hai; passive me 'is + V3' lagayein.
explanation: 'A letter' ke saath Simple Present passive me 'is written by Mona' banega.

question: He cut trees with an axe. (Change the Voice)
answers: Trees were cut by him with an axe.
hint: 'He cut' Past Indefinite tense hai (kyunki Present hota toh 'cuts' likha hota), aur 'Trees' plural hai.
explanation: Past Indefinite aur plural subject 'Trees' hone ke karan 'were cut by him with an axe' sahi passive form hai.

question: Suresh wrote a letter. (Change the Voice)
answers: A letter was written by Suresh.
hint: 'wrote' Past Indefinite (V2) hai; passive me 'was/were + V3' lagta hai.
explanation: Past Indefinite passive structure ke anusaar 'A letter was written by Suresh' sahi jawab hai.

question: She hid the keys. (Change the Voice)
answers: The keys were hidden by her.
hint: 'hid' Past Indefinite hai, 'the keys' plural hai, aur 'hide' ki V3 'hidden' hoti hai.
explanation: Plural object 'The keys' ke saath Past Indefinite passive me 'were hidden by her' ka use hoga.

question: The boy said, "Mohan is writing a letter." (Change the Narration)
answers: The boy said that Mohan was writing a letter.
hint: Reporting verb 'said' past me hai, isliye Present Continuous ('is writing') Past Continuous ('was writing') me badlega.
explanation: Indirect speech me inverted commas hatakar 'that' lagayein aur 'is writing' ko 'was writing' me badlein.

question: The teacher said to us, "The earth revolves around the sun." (Change into indirect speech)
answers: The teacher told us that the earth revolves around the sun.
hint: Universal truth (sarvbhaumik satya) wale sentences ka tense Indirect speech me kabhi nahi badalta.
explanation: 'said to' ko 'told' me badlein, lekin 'The earth revolves around the sun' ek universal truth hai isliye iska tense same rahega.

question: The boy said to me, "I have won the match." (Change the Narration)
answers: The boy told me that he had won the match.
hint: 'I' subject ('The boy') ke anusaar 'he' me badlega aur Present Perfect ('have won') Past Perfect ('had won') ho jayega.
explanation: 'said to me' ka 'told me' banega, 'I' ka 'he' hoga, aur 'have won' ka tense badalkar 'had won' ho jayega.

question: I bought a book. The book was published in Germany. (Combine using a Relative clause)
answers: I bought a book which was published in Germany.
I bought a book that was published in Germany.
I bought a book which/that was published in Germany.
hint: Nirjeev vastu ('a book') ko jodne ke liye relative pronoun 'which' ya 'that' ka use hota hai.
explanation: 'a book' ek non-living thing hai, isliye doosre sentence ke 'The book' ko hatakar 'which' ya 'that' se joda jayega.

question: The girl is in blue dress. The girl is my sister. (Combine into an Adjective clause)
answers: The girl who is in blue dress is my sister.
The girl who is in a blue dress is my sister.
hint: Vyakti ('The girl') ko subject ke roop me jodne ke liye relative pronoun 'who' lagta hai.
explanation: 'The girl' ke baad relative pronoun 'who' lagakar adjective clause 'who is in blue dress' banaya jayega.

question: The lady is a doctor. She is wearing a red dress. (Combine using a Relative Clause)
answers: The lady who is wearing a red dress is a doctor.
hint: 'She' ki jagah 'who' lagayein aur is clause ko 'The lady' ke turant baad rakhein.
explanation: 'The lady' vyakti hai isliye 'She' ko 'who' se badalkar 'The lady who is wearing a red dress is a doctor' banega.

question: My brother is a doctor. He always wears white clothes. (Combine using a Relative Clause)
answers: My brother, who is a doctor, always wears white clothes.
My brother who is a doctor always wears white clothes.
hint: Vyakti ('My brother') ke baare me extra jankari jodne ke liye 'who' ka use karein.
explanation: 'My brother' vyakti hai isliye relative pronoun 'who' ke saath 'My brother, who is a doctor, always wears white clothes' sahi hai.

question: He replied that he would come. (Write the Noun clause from this sentence)
answers: that he would come
He replied that he would come.
hint: Verb ('replied') ke baad 'kya' (what) ka jawab dene wala hissa Noun Clause hota hai.
explanation: 'He replied' ke baad 'that he would come' verb ke object ka kaam kar raha hai, isliye yahi Noun Clause hai.

question: He replied that he would return soon. (Identify the clause 'that he would return soon')
answers: Noun Clause
Noun
hint: Yeh clause verb 'replied' ka object ban kar aa raha hai.
explanation: 'that he would return soon' verb 'replied' ke object ki tarah kaam kar raha hai, isliye yeh Noun Clause hai.

question: Do it before you forget. (Name the clause 'before you forget')
answers: Adverb Clause of Time
Adverb Clause
hint: 'before' samay (time) ko darshata hai ('kab karna hai?').
explanation: 'before you forget' kaam karne ka samay bata raha hai, isliye yeh Adverb Clause of Time hai.

question: She cannot afford it. She buys a car. (Combine using a non-finite clause)
answers: Not being able to afford it, she buys a car.
Not being able to afford it she buys a car.
hint: 'cannot afford' ko participle phrase 'Not being able to afford' me badal kar dono sentences jodein.
explanation: Non-finite clause banate waqt 'She cannot afford it' ko 'Not being able to afford it,' me badal kar 'she buys a car' se joda jata hai.

question: We did it. (Change into Negative)
answers: We did not do it.
We didn't do it.
hint: Yahan 'did' main verb (V2) hai; negative banate waqt helping verb 'did not' ke baad main verb ki V1 ('do') lagana zaroori hai.
explanation: Past Indefinite ke negative me 'did not + V1' lagta hai, isliye 'We did not do it' sahi jawab hai ('do' lagana na bhulein).

question: She put the glass on the table. (Change into Negative)
answers: She did not put the glass on the table.
She didn't put the glass on the table.
hint: 'She put' Past Indefinite hai (agar Present hota toh 'puts' hota), isliye negative me 'did not + V1' lagega.
explanation: Subject 'She' ke saath 'put' likha hai jo V2 (Past) hai, isliye negative banate waqt 'did not put' ka use hoga.

question: He teaches English. (Make Negative)
answers: He does not teach English.
He doesn't teach English.
hint: Present Indefinite me singular subject ('He') ke saath 'does not + V1' lagta hai.
explanation: 'teaches' se 'es' hatakar 'does not teach' likhne par sahi negative sentence banega.

question: He did his work. / You did it nicely. / He did the job very well. (Make Negative)
answers: He did not do his work. / You did not do it nicely. / He did not do the job very well.
He did not do his work.
He didn't do his work.
hint: Teeno sentences Past Indefinite me hain jahan 'did' main verb hai; negative me har jagah 'did not do' aayega.
explanation: Past Indefinite me 'did' ko negative banane ke liye 'did not' ke saath verb ki first form 'do' lagayi jati hai.

question: The students should have submitted the homework on time. (Change into Negative)
answers: The students should not have submitted the homework on time.
The students shouldn't have submitted the homework on time.
hint: Do helping verbs ('should' aur 'have') aane par 'not' hamesha pehle auxiliary verb ('should') ke turant baad lagta hai.
explanation: 'should have' ka negative 'should not have' hota hai, isliye 'should not have submitted' sahi hai.

question: Our team won the match. (Change into Past Perfect Tense)
answers: Our team had won the match.
hint: Past Perfect Tense ka structure: Subject + had + V3 + Object.
explanation: Past Perfect me 'had' ke saath verb ki third form ('won') lagti hai, isliye 'Our team had won the match' sahi hai.

question: They are playing cricket. (Rewrite in Present Perfect Tense)
answers: They have played cricket.
hint: Present Perfect Tense structure: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object ('They' ke saath 'have' lagta hai).
explanation: Plural subject 'They' ke saath Present Perfect me 'have' aur 'play' ki V3 'played' ('They have played cricket') aayegi.

question: Metal / lead / is / than / other / any / heavier /. (Rearrange into a meaningful sentence)
answers: Lead is heavier than any other metal.
hint: Comparative degree structure: Subject + is + comparative adjective + than + any other + singular noun.
explanation: Shabdon ko sahi kram me rakhne par 'Lead is heavier than any other metal.' ek arthpurna comparative vakya banta hai.

question: best / the / policy / is / honesty /. (Rearrange to make a meaningful sentence)
answers: Honesty is the best policy.
hint: Yeh ek prasiddh kahavat (proverb) hai jo 'Honesty' se shuru hoti hai.
explanation: Sahi kram me rakhne par prasiddh kahavat 'Honesty is the best policy.' banti hai.

question: They did not like him. They did not talk to him. (Join using 'neither...nor')
answers: They neither liked him nor talked to him.
hint: 'did not' hatakar dono verbs ko Past Indefinite (V2: 'liked' aur 'talked') me badlein aur 'neither...nor' se jodein.
explanation: 'neither...nor' khud negative hai isliye 'did not' hat jayega aur Past tense banaye rakhne ke liye 'liked' aur 'talked' (V2) aayega.

question: That he is a doctor is certain. (Rewrite the sentence with 'it')
answers: It is certain that he is a doctor.
hint: Sentence ki shuruat 'It is certain' se karein aur uske baad 'that he is a doctor' jodein.
explanation: 'It' se shuru karne par 'It is certain that he is a doctor.' sahi aur natural sentence structure banta hai.
